name: Data Space for Skills
title: Preparing the European Data Space for Skills
summary: A trusted, human-centred ecosystem for sharing and accessing skills data, laying the ground for the first European Data Space for Skills.
details: The project prepares the future deployment of the data space so that organisations and individuals can exchange skills information with practical benefits in the digital age.

name: AI Factory Luxembourg
title: AI services for Luxembourg businesses
summary: Guides businesses from idea to production: solution building, AI maturity assessments, regulatory sandboxes and data-sharing frameworks.
details: My part follows the skills and labour market of AI, so that training offers keep pace with what companies adopting AI actually need.

name: MOKA
title: Management and completion of dynamic knowledge graphs
partners: LIST, MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship with the ORKG group
summary: Methods to manage the evolution of large knowledge graphs, and to test how far LLMs can help maintain them.
details: MOKA identifies and characterises the changes a knowledge graph undergoes when its domain evolves, represents that evolution in a Historical Knowledge Graph, and explores LLM support for maintenance.

name: D4H
title: Deep data science of digital history
partners: LIST with the University of Luxembourg
summary: Knowledge graphs and LLMs that detect how the meaning of words changes over time in historical documents.
details: We formally define three kinds of semantic change and build algorithms to detect them: a meaning that becomes broader or narrower, one that turns pejorative or positive, and one that moves into metaphoric or metonymic use.

name: HKG4COVID
title: Historical knowledge graph of COVID-19
summary: Added the time dimension to COVID-19 knowledge graphs, so the evolution of what we knew about the disease can be followed.
details: Existing graphs only captured the current state of knowledge. HKG4COVID kept its history, giving a view of how understanding of the disease developed.

name: Dynaccurate
title: Maintenance of dynamic terminologies
summary: A web application that keeps data annotations correct as terminologies evolve. The result of seven years of research, it became a spin-off company.
details: Legacy data stays annotated with the current version of a terminology, which preserves its value and removes out-of-date references. I was a lead designer and developer of the technology.

name: ELISA
title: Evolution of semantic annotations
summary: Tools that understand how ontologies evolve and repair the semantic annotations that depend on them.
details: Annotations are updated directly when they can be modified; otherwise a query-enrichment mechanism reflects the ontology's evolution so annotated data remains searchable. Two life-science cases served as testbeds.

name: METIS
title: Knowledge representation for clinical guidelines
summary: Formal models of clinical guidelines that detect conflicts between treatments for patients with several conditions.
details: The project identified what knowledge is needed to reason about guidelines, formalised interaction rules in a reusable way, and implemented them with Semantic Web technologies and medical Linked Open Data.

name: SACCOM
title: Self-adaptation of collaborative medical systems
summary: Ontologies, big data and IoT for diabetes care: treatment plans that adapt as the patient's state and environment change.
details: Treatment plans and their goals were described with standard terminologies such as SNOMED CT and ICD, and autonomic-computing algorithms reconfigured medical services to personalise care.

name: DYNAMO
title: Reconciliation of dynamic medical knowledge organisation systems
summary: A formal framework that repairs mappings between medical terminologies when a new version is released, without recomputing them all.
details: It takes into account the kind of change affecting each element and the nature of the existing mappings, so the mappings that a release invalidates are adapted automatically.
